brief:
**BLUF:** Bluefield, WV police are actively seeking Hallie Graham on serious felony warrants tied to an early Saturday incident at a local saloon; she is considered armed and dangerous. A major fish-farm project spanning Russell and Tazewell counties has been placed on pause. Appalachian Power’s proposed base-rate increase, which could add about $9.10 monthly to typical residential bills, heads to public hearing later this month.

## LAW ENFORCEMENT AND COURTS
Bluefield, WV police are seeking the public’s help locating **Hallie Graham**, who faces active warrants for first-degree attempted murder, three counts of wanton endangerment, and malicious assault. The charges stem from an alleged incident early Saturday morning (Oct. 3–4) at Wild Riders Saloon in Mercer County. Graham is considered armed and dangerous; the public is advised not to approach her. Information should be reported to Bluefield Police at (304) 327-6101 (option 1) or 911. Patrolman P.S. Mullins is the investigator.[[1]](https://www.wvva.com/2026/10/04/woman-wanted-attempted-murder-following-alleged-saturday-saloon-incident/)[[2]](https://woay.com/bluefield-police-asks-for-publics-help-in-locating-woman-wanted-on-attempted-murder-and-assault-charges/)[[3]](https://www.lootpress.com/armed-and-dangerous-woman-wanted-for-attempted-murder-following-incident-at-mercer-county-saloon/)

Nothing else reported in the last 24 hours from Tazewell County Sheriff’s Office, Virginia State Police Division IV, Richlands/Tazewell/Bluefield VA police, or Southwest Virginia Regional Jail.

## FIRE, EMS AND RESCUE
Nothing reported in the last 24 hours.

## HAZARDS, WEATHER AND ROADS
Nothing reported in the last 24 hours. NWS alerts: none active.

## GOVERNMENT AND POLITICS
Appalachian Power is seeking Virginia State Corporation Commission approval for a base-rate increase that would add roughly $9.10 per month (5.4%) to the bill of a typical residential customer using 1,000 kWh. The proposal would generate an additional $61.4 million annually for the utility. A public hearing is scheduled for Oct. 19 (register by Oct. 15); an evidentiary hearing follows on Oct. 20, with a final decision due by Jan. 15, 2027. New rates could not take effect before March 1.[[4]](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/virginia-hear-appalachian-power-rate-045200287.html)[[5]](https://cardinalnews.org/2026/10/01/regulators-prepare-to-hear-appalachian-powers-case-for-raising-rates/)

## OTHER LOCAL
Pure Salmon has halted or paused work on its planned fish farm project spanning Russell and Tazewell counties, citing tariffs and gas prices.[[6]](https://virginiabusiness.com/southwest-fish-farm-fights-the-currents/)

The Richlands Fire Department will host an open house on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, from 11 a.m.–2 p.m. at 110 Kents Ridge Road (Brickyard Addition), with hot dogs, ice cream, and activities.[[7]](https://x.com/TownOfRichlands/status/2107129210485498157)

## WATCH -- NEXT 48 HOURS
- Oct. 10: Richlands Fire Department open house (11 a.m.–2 p.m.).
- Oct. 15: Deadline to register for Appalachian Power rate-hike public hearing.
- Oct. 19: Virginia SCC public hearing on Appalachian Power base-rate case.
